$comment: Bundled defaults for agent-signatures.json (DESIGN §6-4). Seeded into <app-data>/agent-signatures.json on first run; your edits there are merged over these per agent key and hot-reloaded within ~2s. Patterns are Rust `regex` crate syntax, matched against one visible (ANSI-stripped) line of terminal output. A pattern that fails to compile is skipped with a warning and never disables the rest. Precedence is by CLASS, not by line: the whole visible tail is searched for a `waiting` match, then for `working`, then for `idle` (DESIGN §6-4), so a broad `idle` pattern that also matches a line still on screen during a turn is safe. Verified against captured streams in src-tauri/tests/fixtures/streams (claude 2.1.263, codex 0.145.0, 2026-09-07). A seeded copy that has never been edited is rewritten when this file changes (agents/signatures.rs SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_DIGESTS); an edited copy is never touched.
$comment_v2: v2 (BACKLOG M1.5 #2, 2026-09-08): every one of these CLIs blocks on a selection menu whose only marker is its footer — claude 'Enter to select · ↑/↓ to navigate · Esc to cancel', codex 'Press enter to continue'. The v1 `waiting` sets only knew the yes/no wordings, so a menu read as `idle`. The menu-row patterns require the highlighted-row cursor (`❯`/`›`) before the ordinal so that a numbered list in ordinary output cannot pose as a prompt.
$comment_v3: v3 (BACKLOG M1.5 15b, 2026-09-09): claude's full-screen views (/help and the other alternate-screen panels) close on Esc and say so in their footer — 'Esc to close' was the one wording the v2 waiting set did not know. The engine no longer depends on that line alone: a quiet alternate screen with a low-CPU foreground group is WaitingForInput on the strength of those three observations (status/engine.rs, DESIGN §6-4), and this pattern is what gives that state a prompt worth quoting.
